text:
maria: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout we see ~12% drop in prefix cache hit on a private customer env (VPC + netstore). noticed during nightly perf job.

sam: ugh, timeline? which commit/rollout id?

maria: rollout id rwd-kernel-2026-03-16, service runtime v2.8.3 -> v2.9.0. repro in staging private with smaller trace set.

lee: is this only private? hosted/dedicated look fine?

maria: hosted + dedicated stable, private shows both lower hit-rate and higher kv fetch p50 (from ~6ms to ~28ms).

oliver: could be netstore latency exposing keying differences — if our key normalization was relying on local clock/sequence bundling it could miss matches when responses are reordered.

anya: I ran a quick profile. attaching snippet:

```
# kv-client latency histogram (private)
p50: 28.4ms
p90: 120.2ms
p99: 430.6ms
# cache hit-rate per-prefix
prefix:A    78% -> 66%
prefix:B    84% -> 73%
```

sam: can you paste the exact cache key proto for a failing request? we need to see salt/sequence/len.

maria: here — sanitized: `prefix=v1:user:prompt-hash=3f9a...:len=256:kernel=attn-optimized-v2` — in private the kernel label is sometimes `attn-v2-fused` after selector changes.

oliver: that kernel label difference will make cache keys different unless we canonicalize kernel label out of the key. Did selector start emitting explicit kernel tag?

anya: yes, selector now annotates chosen kernel for telemetry. we wanted visibility for perf but forgot to make kernel tag excluded from cache key. regression introduced in 2f4b7c.

lee: so hosted/dedicated didn't show because the kernel tag was identical across nodes there, but private's netstore + heterogeneous hardware caused selectors to pick different kernel names -> key entropy increased -> lower hit-rate.

maria: exactly. combined with slightly higher netstore latency that pushed more requests past expiry window we get compounded misses.

sam: action items: 1) hotfix: stop including kernel tag in cache key generation or add normalization map. 2) add a unit test for key canonicalization. 3) add a canary that simulates mixed-kernel labels.

oliver: I'll open a PR to strip kernel label from stable cache key (WIP). also propose a migration: accept both old and new keys for 24h to avoid cold-start storm.

anya: also we should add an integration test that runs cache-key collision simulation with netstore delays (simulate p50=30ms, p90=200ms). I'll add a perf test to CI.

infra-bot: deploy v2.9.1-hotfix started for runtime service (tracking: deploy/1976543222).

sam: nice. can we also add logging that reports "key normalization diff" counts per deployment-type so we can detect config drift earlier?

maria: yes — will add a per-deployment metric: cache_key_variants_count and a small dashboard.

lee: long term we should avoid mutable metadata in keys. kernel selection telemetry is valuable but belongs in separate metadata header not key.

oliver: agreed. putting kernel id into request metadata + tag the trace instead. keys should be deterministic across selections.

anya: note for private deployments: network store timeouts + clock skew can amplify these issues. let's document recommended netstore timeouts and suggest conservative TTLs for private.

maria: repro steps I used for staging private: `./scripts/perf/repro_cache_warmup.sh --prefixes 200 --mix 80/20 --netstore-latency 30` — output: `.reports/hitrates-1976543210.tsv`

sam: thanks. once hotfix is live we should run the nightly perf job again and post before/after hit-rate numbers here. good catch. :thumbsup:

maria: will update thread when deploy finishes and after the nightly run.

infra-bot: deploy v2.9.1-hotfix successful on staging (1976543265).

maria: staging results: overall prefix hit-rate recovered from 68% -> 83% in the simulated private. posting full CSV to GCS: gs://rwd-perf/reports/1976543210-postfix.csv

sam: excellent. let's get the PR merged, but keep the normalization test and the canary in place before GA.

maria: noted. thanks everyone.
